name: Cicatridine

lead: Cicatridine is a French pharmacy brand built on hyaluronic acid, a molecule found in skin that supports wound repair. It is sold in several forms, including a topical gel containing almond oil and vaginal ovules.
For appearance, the relevant use is scar care: a 2026 observational study compared it with another gel on post-cesarean scar cosmetic results.

paras: The topical form is applied to the healing wound area twice a day in the study setting [1]. Scar products are typically used for weeks after the wound closes.

Hyaluronic acid is a common skincare ingredient with a good tolerability record in the studies reviewed; individual reactions are possible, and a doctor should assess any wound that is not healing normally.

angle.text: People use the topical form on surgical wounds hoping for a tidier scar. The study that examined cosmetic results compared it with another gel.

lead: Cicatridine is a French pharmacy product line based on hyaluronic acid (HA), with a topical gel containing synthetic and natural compounds such as almond oil and vaginal ovules [1][2]. HA is a major component of skin and supports re-epithelialisation as wounds heal [3].

In appearance terms, it is used for scar care. A 2026 retrospective observational study in Romania compared a natural-compound gel containing Centella asiatica and aloe vera with Cicatridine in 50 patients each, evaluating the cosmetic results of post-cesarean scars [1].

Most published work is gynaecological. A 2008 controlled clinical study of 319 women found cervical repair after surgery was more frequent with Cicatridine ovules than controls [4], and a 2011 paper reported faster healing and improved quality of life in post-radiotherapy lesions [5].
infobox: Hyaluronic acid; almond oil in the gel

paras: The topical gel was used twice daily in a post-cesarean scar comparison [1]. Hyaluronic acid is common in skincare products, though its evaluation in those products is limited [3].
Ovules have been studied for healing after cervical procedures and brachytherapy, and for vulvar dystrophy as a cream [4][5].
HA supports keratinocyte proliferation and migration and is found at wound margins; a 2023 review reported limited positive clinical evidence for HA in surgical skin repair [3].

A 2026 retrospective study compared Reparis with Cicatridine on post-cesarean scar cosmetic measures in 100 patients [1]. A 2008 open, non-randomised controlled study (319 women) reported repair of the cervix in 93% versus 70% at six weeks and 99% versus 89% at three months after surgery, and 86% versus 0% after brachytherapy [4]. A 2026 prospective study of 121 women using Cicatridine ovules for 14 days found epithelial transformation rising to 82.9% at three months [2]. A 2011 paper reported over 90% of patients responded to HA cream for vulvar dystrophy [5].
